description: I am looking for motivated team members with skills in programming, AI, engineering, scientific research, and design who are passionate about space and innovation. Together, we can turn creative ideas into impactful solutions!
summary: SENTRIX is an AI-assisted Earth Surface Intelligence Platform that transforms satellite radar observations into understandable environmental information. Using NASA–ISRO NISAR data, SENTRIX aims to detect and visualize changes on Earth’s surface through satellite comparison, interactive mapping and AI-assisted insights. It also incorporates supporting information from UAE NCM, Windy and NASA GPM to help explore environmental conditions. Our project directly addresses NASA Space Apps Challenge 06, Dancing with the SARs, by making NISAR observations easier to explore and understand. Initially focusing on water and wetland monitoring in the UAE, SENTRIX aims to support environmental awareness, research and better-informed decisions.
details:
SENTRIX is a project we created because we wanted to find a way to understand how our planet changes using satellite technology. We noticed that satellite data contains a lot of useful information, but it can be difficult for ordinary people to understand. We wanted to make that information easier to explore and more meaningful.

Our idea is to build an interactive platform that uses NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite data to observe and compare changes on Earth's surface over time. Users can select a location, explore available satellite observations, and view changes through an interactive map. We are especially interested in monitoring water and wetland changes in the UAE. We also plan to use weather information from the UAE National Center of Meteorology (NCM), Windy, and NASA GPM to provide additional context and help users better understand environmental conditions.

We are developing our prototype using Lovable, with interactive mapping and geospatial technologies to support the platform. Our goal is to bring satellite data, weather information, maps, and AI-assisted explanations together in one place.

What makes SENTRIX special is that we are not just showing satellite images. We want to help people understand what they are looking at and why the changes might matter. We hope the platform can be useful for students, researchers, and people interested in protecting the environment.

While developing our idea, we considered the accuracy of the data, the reliability of our sources, ease of use, and the limitations of satellite observations. We also understand that a change in radar data does not always mean a specific environmental event has happened, so our results need to be interpreted carefully.

Our vision is to make Earth observation easier for everyone and encourage people to use technology to better understand and care for our planet.
